mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns due to accommodative monetary policy reducing equity discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS < 3.0% periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to heightened recession risks and reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in UNRATE > 4.5% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 0.5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises by more than 0.25% in the last month, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to aggressive monetary tightening and inflation concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in the joint condition (CPIAUCSL>0.5% m/m AND FEDFUNDS>0.25% m/m) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime defined by GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.5% annualized and unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns due to strong economic fundamentals and investor confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1>2.5% annualized AND UNRATE<4.0%) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns due to strong current economic activity and positive momentum in the real economy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns in INDPRO above 12-month MA periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to rising inflation expectations and potential accelerated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in CPIAUCSL > 3.5% (y/y) periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1300 thousand units and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to confluence of weak housing demand and deteriorating labor market conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in the joint condition (HOUST<1300 AND UNRATE>4.0%) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the recessionary regime defined by unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.0% and industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns due to severe economic contraction and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in the recessionary regime (UNRATE>5.0% AND INDPRO<100) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
